questions.prompt: For the member using a walking aid, what should the organiser do?

options.A: Assume every part of the standard route is suitable.
options.C: Discuss requirements and request an adapted route.

questions.explanation: The centre can discuss an accessible section and limits rather than promise all paths or cancel automatically.

questions.prompt: Where can the group eat its own packed lunch?

options.A: In a shared covered picnic area.
options.B: At privately reserved picnic tables guaranteed to be empty.
options.C: Only in the cafe after booking its menu.

questions.explanation: The picnic area accepts visitors' food but is shared.

questions.prompt: How are photographic observation points selected?

options.A: Visitors may move barriers if they need a closer view.
options.B: The guide selects permitted points for the conditions.
options.C: Every booking includes access to nesting areas.

questions.explanation: The guide controls appropriate points; restricted areas remain restricted.

questions.prompt: What should the group do if heavy rain is forecast?

options.B: Let individual members make separate assumptions.
options.C: Wait for a direct message about the plan.

questions.explanation: The outdoor section may be adapted; only some conditions require cancellation.

questions.prompt: If a guided route changes, visitors should

options.A: leave to follow the original route alone.
options.C: assume the whole visit has lost its value.

questions.explanation: A current adaptation can itself offer learning; the map cannot show every short-term condition.

questions.prompt: When comparing display photographs, what should visitors consider?

options.A: The dates and conditions under which images were made.
options.C: Every visual difference as definite long-term change.

questions.explanation: Season, weather and viewpoint can explain contrasts.

questions.prompt: What makes an uncertain identification useful?

options.A: Presenting an app suggestion as independent recognition.
options.B: Reporting a confident name without details.
options.C: Describing observed features and how a suggested name was obtained.

questions.explanation: The report should separate observation, identification and uncertainty.

questions.prompt: Volunteer monitoring differs from an ordinary visit because it

options.A: includes everybody on the tour automatically.
options.B: requires a consistent method and training.
options.C: values the largest number of observations regardless of quality.

questions.explanation: Monitoring has its own method, training and participation process.

questions.prompt: What feedback is most useful?

options.A: A specific location or instruction that caused difficulty.
options.B: A demand to make everything better without an example.
options.C: A complaint sent after departure as an urgent same-day request.

questions.explanation: Specific examples help the centre identify what needs changing.

questions.prompt: Which TWO fixed-choice questions do the students retain?

options.A: How visitors heard about the centre before visiting
options.B: How many species visitors think live at the site
options.D: Which information visitors used to find a route after arrival

scoring.rule: One point per distinct correct choice. Duplicate choices never earn a second point. More than two submitted choices is an invalid response requiring correction, not automatic full credit.

questions.explanation: The chosen questions concern information before and during the visit; knowledge, camera price and address do not serve that aim.

options.D: Changing which passing visitors are approached

scoring.rule: One point per distinct correct choice. Duplicate choices never earn a second point. More than two submitted choices is an invalid response requiring correction, not automatic full credit.

questions.explanation: Changed wording changes the meaning of responses; changed recruitment changes the invited sample.
